### Problem: Find if Path Exists in Graph {#sec-gr-p2-path}

Undirected graph, $n$ vertices labelled $0..n-1$, edges `edges[i] = [u, v]`. Return whether `source` can reach `destination`.

**Graph model.** Undirected. Both directions go into the lists. $n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$, so the search is a queue or an explicit stack, and the store is lists.

**Invariants.** `source == destination` is true before any edge is read: the trivial walk has length $0$. A vertex enters the queue at most once.

**Approaches.**

1. **Breadth-first search** — mark on push, return when the destination is popped. $O(n + m)$.
2. **Disjoint sets** — union every edge, then compare the roots of the two endpoints. Same asymptotics, and it answers every pair once the unions are done. The chapter on disjoint sets develops the structure; the form here is only the connectivity test.

#### Breadth-first search

::: {.form-next}
Mark the source, then mark a neighbour at the moment it is pushed. Stop when the destination comes off the queue.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("path", "bfs")
    assert str(final) == "True"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def valid_path(n, edges, source, destination):
    if source == destination:
        return True
    adj = undirected(n, edges, one=False)
    seen = [False] * n
    seen[source] = True
    q = deque([source])
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        for v in adj[u]:
            if seen[v]:
                continue
            if v == destination:
                return True
            seen[v] = True
            q.append(v)
    return False


assert valid_path(3, [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 0]], 0, 2) is True
assert valid_path(6, [[0, 1], [0, 2], [3, 5], [5, 4], [4, 3]], 0, 5) is False
assert valid_path(1, [], 0, 0) is True
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool validPath(int n, vector<vector<int>>& edges, int source, int destination) {
    if (source == destination) return true;
    vector<vector<int>> adj(n);
    for (auto& e : edges) {
        adj[e[0]].push_back(e[1]);
        adj[e[1]].push_back(e[0]);
    }
    vector<char> seen(n);
    queue<int> q;
    q.push(source);
    seen[source] = 1;
    while (!q.empty()) {
        int u = q.front();
        q.pop();
        for (int v : adj[u]) {
            if (seen[v]) continue;
            if (v == destination) return true;
            seen[v] = 1;
            q.push(v);
        }
    }
    return false;
}
```

:::

#### Disjoint sets

::: {.form-next}
Join the two ends of every edge. The source reaches the destination when they finish in the same component.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("path", "dsu")
    assert str(final) == "True"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def valid_path_dsu(n, edges, source, destination):
    parent = list(range(n))

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    for u, v in edges:
        a, b = find(u), find(v)
        if a != b:
            parent[a] = b
    return find(source) == find(destination)


assert valid_path_dsu(3, [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 0]], 0, 2) is True
assert valid_path_dsu(6, [[0, 1], [0, 2], [3, 5], [5, 4], [4, 3]], 0, 5) is False
for n in range(1, 10):
    for _ in range(25):
        edges = [[i, j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n) if random.random() < 0.3]
        s, t = random.randrange(n), random.randrange(n)
        assert valid_path(n, edges, s, t) is valid_path_dsu(n, edges, s, t)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int find(vector<int>& parent, int x) {
    while (parent[x] != x) {
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]];
        x = parent[x];
    }
    return x;
}

bool validPathDsu(int n, vector<vector<int>>& edges, int source, int destination) {
    vector<int> parent(n);
    iota(parent.begin(), parent.end(), 0);
    for (auto& e : edges) {
        int a = find(parent, e[0]), b = find(parent, e[1]);
        if (a != b) parent[a] = b;
    }
    return find(parent, source) == find(parent, destination);
}
```

:::

:::

**Worked trace.** First sample: $0$ pushes $1$, $1$ pushes $2$, and $2$ is the destination. Second sample: $0$ pushes $1$ and $2$, the queue empties, and $5$ was never marked.

**Edge cases.** One vertex, source and destination both $0$. Two vertices and no edge, source different from destination. A triangle, every pair reachable.

**Pitfalls.** Storing a directed edge one way on an undirected statement splits the triangle into a path and reports the wrong way as unreachable. A recursive search on $n = 2 \cdot 10^5$ along a path overflows. Leaving the source unmarked lets the walk push it from its first neighbour.

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- **One direction only.** Both official samples still pass if each undirected edge is stored once. Source $1$ and destination $2$ on the second graph is the catch: the path is $1 - 0 - 2$, and vertex $1$ has an empty list.
- **The trivial walk.** A test that looks only at newly discovered neighbours returns false when `source == destination`, including the single vertex.
- **A matrix at this limit.** $n = 2 \cdot 10^5$ does not fit an adjacency matrix, and scanning a row is quadratic. Lists are linear in the input.
- **Recursion on a long path.** A recursive search passes the samples and dies on a path of length $2 \cdot 10^5$. The queue, or an explicit stack, is the search that fits.
:::

**Variants.** One-way portals are [CF 500A · New Year Transportation](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/500/A){rating="1000"}: store the arc once, and the walk is a single chain. Many connectivity questions on one fixed graph are one search per unmarked vertex, then a label comparison. Edges that arrive between questions are the disjoint-set form above. A blocked vertex is marked seen before the search starts. Printing a path is a parent pointer written at the moment the vertex is marked.

Source: [LC 1971 · Find if Path Exists in Graph](https://leetcode.com/problems/find-if-path-exists-in-graph/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
